Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: New, painless swelling of the left elbow noted ~1 week ago while showering; no recalled trauma.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Stable over the week; warmth but no significant change in size or pain.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial / lip / tongue / uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, or neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: No prior similar elbow episodes; no prior ED or hospital care for this.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Peanut allergy (severity and reaction details not documented).  
  • No known drug allergies.  
  • No regular medications.  
- Any relevant social context: Works a desk job; physically active (runs 2–3 times/week).

Objective:
- Observable swelling: Mild swelling over left olecranon bursa; skin appears dry; area described and visually confirmed as slightly warm.
- Airway/breathing: Normal; no respiratory distress reported or observed.
- Mental status: Alert, oriented, conversational.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person: Not stated.

Assessment:
- Likely left olecranon bursitis (non-septic) — warm, fluctuant swelling without significant pain or systemic features; no trauma history; stable for 1 week.
- Differential considerations (to be evaluated with labs): crystal arthropathy (gout), inflammatory arthropathy, infection (septic bursitis/arthritis considered but less likely).
- Peanut allergy noted (no current reaction).

Plan:
- Pharmacologic: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily after food (OTC); stop if heartburn occurs. (dose/route/frequency documented as advised)
- Diagnostics: Arrange blood tests (inflammatory markers, infection markers, rheumatologic antibodies, uric acid) — forms to be mailed to patient; obtain blood draw promptly.
- Follow-up: Virtual or in-person review approximately 6 days after blood draw to reassess elbow and review results.
- Escalation criteria/red flags explained: If elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, or redness spreads/intensifies, patient to contact service immediately for urgent assessment (possible septic arthritis).
- Additional instructions: Maintain normal activity as tolerated; monitor size/warmth of swelling; choose follow-up mode (face-to-face or video) based on convenience and symptom course.
- Allergy management: No epinephrine auto-injector discussed; no acute allergic issues today.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  – Detailed description of peanut allergy reaction severity and management plan.  
  – Medication list confirmation (none noted but not reconciled with pharmacy records).  
  – Auto-injector availability/education for known peanut allergy.  
  – Exact elbow circumference/size, presence/absence of fluctuant fluid on palpation.  
  – Vitals (temperature, HR, BP) to better exclude systemic infection.
● Internal conflicts:
  – DOB 5 Apr 1973 suggests age 50, but patient stated age 53 (conflict noted).
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; full clinical content captured.
